title: On a ramp, part of the weight pulls the object down the slope
summary: On a slope, part of an object's weight pulls it along the ramp, and friction can push back up the ramp.
body: OpenStax Physics says that on an incline, the weight splits into a part perpendicular to the surface and a part parallel to the surface. The parallel part makes the object accelerate down the incline. Friction opposes that motion, so it acts up the plane. The perpendicular part is balanced by the normal force when the object is not accelerating into the surface. Urone and Hinrichs, 26 March 2020. A steeper ramp gives a larger downhill part. The page is the textbook split of the weight, not a building code for ramps.
